item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: SpaceXAI subprocessor admin setting
item.description:
Updated October 28, 2026: Starting in early November, Grok 4.6 will be available through usage-based billing in Copilot Chat for eligible Frontier customers who have enabled the SpaceXAI subprocessor setting. 

Please refer to the original message below for subprocessor/Grok eligibility. Eligible users must have usage-based billing enabled to access Grok 4.6. Please refer to MC1519122 for more information on how to set up usage-based billing for models in Chat.

[What and why:]

As part of our efforts to expand model choice in Copilot, SpaceXAI has been added to Microsoft's Online Services Subprocessor List, published in the Service Trust Portal. Being listed as a subprocessor does not, by itself, mean SpaceXAI is enabled for your organization or that SpaceXAI is processing your data.

Access to Grok models is governed by a new SpaceXAI admin setting under AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The setting is disabled by default. Eligible customers participating in Frontier must explicitly enable the setting before Grok models can be used in their organization. If enabled, Grok models will be available in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Users can select Grok from the model selector when using Copilot in those apps.

When the SpaceXAI setting is enabled, Microsoft’s Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply to the use of Grok models, except as otherwise disclosed in Microsoft Learn documentation.

[Rollout schedule:]

The SpaceXAI setting to enable the use of Grok models in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint will be available to eligible customers starting September 18, 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Customers participating in Frontier are eligible to access Grok models in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Note: The following customers are not eligible and won’t see the SpaceXAI admin setting during initial rollout even if participating in Frontier.
  • Tenants in the EU, EFTA, and the UK.
  • Government cloud customers (GCC, GCC High, DoD).
  • Administrators managing model access controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • The SpaceXAI admin setting will become available to eligible Frontier customers and will be disabled by default. Grok models are not available, and no customer data will be processed by SpaceXAI, unless an admin enables it.
  • If the admin setting is enabled, users will be able to select a Grok model from the model selector when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Admins can scope access to specific users or groups.
  • There is no change for organizations that take no action.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Review Microsoft Learn page covering SpaceXAI as a subprocessor and the new administrative setting.
  • Decide whether to enable the SpaceXAI setting for your organization and determine whether to scope access to specific users or groups.
  • Review published compliance information, including SpaceXAI's via the SpaceXAI Trust Center, and confirm it aligns with your organization's requirements before enabling access.
  • Notify your helpdesk and compliance teams if your organization has specific requirements around third-party model providers.

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance areaImpact
AI/ML or agent capabilitiesIntroduces Grok models as a model option in Copilot for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Admin controlsA new SpaceXAI admin setting lets admins enable or disable access, with user- and group-level scoping. It is disabled by default.
Data processingSpaceXAI is listed as a Microsoft AI subprocessor. No processing occurs unless the setting is enabled.
Regional availabilityOnly available to Frontier Public customers – not available to customers in the EU, EFTA, or UK at this time, or to government clouds.
Third-party certificationsSOC 1 Type II, PCI, FedRAMP and HITRUST certifications are not currently available for SpaceXAI. Customers should review available certification information before enabling access. Refer to SpaceXAI’s own certification landing page to understand the availability of their certifications, additional exclusions, and audit reports.

  2. SpaceXAI as a subprocessor in Microsoft Online Services
  3. Understanding AI functionality and models in Microsoft Online Services

item.title: [stayInformed] Frontier expands to include public previews in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Frontier now covers more of Microsoft 365. Starting in November 2026, users enrolled in Frontier will start getting eligible public preview features in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint, in addition to Copilot.

Instead of looking in different places for previews, admins use one program and one setting to give the users they choose early access across Microsoft 365.

Frontier is optional and controlled by your admins. It is separate from each user's Standard release or Deferred release preference, which still decides when users receive features once they're generally available. If you already have users enrolled in Frontier, they don't need to re-enroll.

Release options in the Microsoft 365 admin center:

  • Frontier (preview access): Opt in specific users and groups, or all users, to get eligible public preview features before general availability.
  • Standard release (general availability): Receive updates as soon as they're generally available. This is the default.
  • Deferred release (general availability): Receive eligible major updates approximately 30 days after Standard release begins, allowing more time for validation and readiness.

Learn more: Get started with the Microsoft Frontier Program

[Rollout Schedule:]

November 2026: Users enrolled in Frontier will start getting eligible public preview features in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint, in addition to Copilot. 

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Frontier makes early access to Microsoft 365 previews simpler and more predictable. Instead of looking in different places for previews, your organization gets eligible public preview features for Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Copilot through one program, managed from one admin setting. Admins choose which users and groups take part, and everyone else stays on their Standard release or Deferred release schedule, so it's clear who gets what and when. 

In November 2026, admins can also manage Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release together in one place in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Early access gives you time to prepare guidance and support teams, and a way to share feedback before features are broadly released.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Users enrolled in Frontier will start seeing eligible preview features in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint, in addition to the Copilot preview features they get today.
  • If your Frontier setting is All users, every user with the right licenses will get these preview features.
  • Users not enrolled in Frontier see no change. They keep getting features based on their Standard release or Deferred release preference.
  • A Microsoft Copilot license is no longer required to enroll users in Frontier. Users need licenses for the products they want to preview. For example, to use Frontier features for Teams, users need a license that includes Microsoft Teams. Enrolled users without that license aren't shown that product's Frontier features.
  • Users in Targeted release aren't automatically enrolled in Frontier.
  • Preview features may change before general availability.
  • Future additions to Frontier will be announced in Message center.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review your current Frontier enrollment. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier. You can choose No access (default), All users, or Specific users and groups.
  • If Frontier is set to All users, decide whether everyone should get preview features. If not, switch to Specific users and groups.
  • If you're new to Frontier, consider starting with a pilot group and expanding over time. A pilot group could be IT staff, an innovation team, or employees who want to test the latest features.
  • If you use Targeted release, enroll the users you want to get preview features in Frontier. Targeted release users aren't enrolled automatically, and Targeted release retires in January 2027.
  • Make sure enrolled users have licenses for the products they will preview.
  • If you use the Microsoft 365 Insider (for business) program to validate production builds, keep doing so. To try eligible preview features offered through Frontier, enroll the users who will participate.
  • Let your helpdesk, change management teams, and pilot groups know that enrolled users will start seeing preview features.

Until the unified release preferences experience is available, admins can continue to manage Frontier enrollment through Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. In November 2026, you can manage Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release together in the unified release preferences experience, or continue to manage Frontier through Copilot settings. For details, see MC1490899.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins manage Frontier enrollment (No access, All users, or Specific users and groups) through Copilot Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Additional Resources:]

  • Frontier expands to more Microsoft 365 public previews | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Get started with the Microsoft Frontier Program
  • Explore AI Early Access in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Frontier

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

Learn more

  • Microsoft’s response to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
  • Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates in Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Copilot Code is rolling out in Frontier
item.description:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Copilot Code is an AI-powered coding experience in Microsoft Copilot that helps people turn ideas into trackers, dashboards, apps, and other solutions using natural language. Work IQ grounds what they build in emails, meetings, documents, chats, and connected data.

People closest to a problem can build the solution they need while your organization maintains control. Published apps run on Copilot Managed Runtime and inherit your organization’s governance, security, and management controls.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Copilot Code: Begins with the Frontier program in late October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users in the Frontier program who have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and are enabled for usage-based billing.
  • Microsoft 365 admins who manage the Copilot app, spending policies, and usage-based billing.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Copilot app on Windows
  • Microsoft Copilot on the web
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Copilot Managed Runtime
  • Work IQ
  • GitHub, when enabled

What users can do with Copilot Code

  • Users access Code from the Copilot app navigation pane and describe what they want to build. Copilot can ask clarifying questions and use their work context to build the solution.
  • Users can refine what they build through conversation or direct edits. On PC, when local coding is enabled, users can also work with local files and tools or use the terminal.
  • Users can publish projects to Copilot Managed Runtime, a Microsoft-managed cloud environment, and share them with others in their organization. Access to underlying data continues to depend on the user's permissions.
  • Users can connect Code to GitHub when the connection is enabled by an admin.

How admin settings control access

Copilot Code uses usage-based billing. To use Copilot Code, users need:

  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • A spending policy.

By default:

  • Cloud coding sessions are enabled on web and PC for eligible users with a Copilot spending policy.
  • Local coding sessions are disabled by default. Admins can allow local coding on PC by setting Code execution location to Cloud and local in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users covered by a spending policy where the setting "Allow new Agents and services as they become available" is enabled automatically receive access to Code through that spending policy.

For more information about Allow new agents and services setting, see MC1470425.

The following settings determine what users see and can use:

Code spending policyAllow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billingCode execution locationWhat users see
AssignedNo effectCloud (default)Code with cloud coding sessions
AssignedNo effectCloud and localCode with cloud coding sessions and local coding sessions on PC
Not assignedOnNo effectCode entry point and welcome page; Code cannot be used

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Action is required if you want eligible users to use Copilot Code.

  1. Review the Copilot Code blog.
  2. Deploy the unified Microsoft Copilot app.
  3. For Windows devices participating in Frontier, set the Microsoft Copilot target channel to Beta.
  4. Review your spending policies and confirm that Code is included for the users who should have access. If automatic access to new usage-based services is enabled, review which users will automatically receive Code through their existing spending policy.
  5. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure the appropriate spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management.
  6. Decide whether users should have cloud-only coding or cloud and local coding. Local coding is off by default.
  7. Prepare your help desk for the new Code experience, including the in-product experience and your organization's access-request process.
  8. Review information about Copilot Managed Runtime.
  9. Review the Frontier program requirements and guidance.

Resources

  • Copilot Code blog
  • Get started with Copilot Code
  • Deploy the unified Microsoft Copilot application | Microsoft Learn
  • Microsoft Copilot update policies for Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Copilot Managed Runtime blog
  • Get started with the Frontier program

[Compliance considerations:]

Stores new customer dataUsers can create projects/apps and publish them to Copilot Managed Runtime.
Changes how existing customer data is accessed or processedCode can use Work IQ, including emails, meetings, documents, chats, and connected data, to ground what users build.
Introduces new user interaction with organizational dataApps built with Code can use organizational context, and published apps may be shared with others in the organization subject to underlying data permissions.
Introduces external/third-party integrationGitHub can optionally be connected when enabled by an admin.
Introduces admin-controlled usage-based billingCode uses usage-based billing and requires the applicable spending policy for users to use the experience.
Introduces local execution/data interactionAdmins can optionally enable local coding sessions on PC, allowing users to work with local files and tools.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 admin center: Usage reports to manage metered consumption costs for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (preview)
item.description:

The new report will roll out in preview. During the preview stage, the report will display a maximum of 30 days of message consumption history. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 490738.

[When this will happen:]

Public Preview: Available now.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in end of April 2027 (previously early January) and expect to complete by end of May 2027 (previously end of January).

[How this will affect your organization:]

After you have set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Copilot, either in the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Microsoft Power Platform admin center, and you have enabled agent usage in your organization, you will see a new report including metrics for messages consumed at the levels of tenant, users, agents, and agent-user. To help you mitigate overspending, you will see alerts when users have consumed more than 2000 billed messages.

This new report will be on by default and will be available in the Microsoft admin center at Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Message consumption:

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Viva: Targeted audience surveys in the Copilot dashboard
item.description:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We're introducing targeted audience surveys in the Copilot dashboard. This feature enables authorized users to launch Microsoft Viva Pulse surveys for predefined Copilot user populations without creating or maintaining recipient lists.

Survey audiences are dynamically based on Copilot dashboard data and can be scoped using existing dashboard filters. This helps organizations gather feedback from Copilot users while reducing administrative effort associated with audience management.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568072.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Beginning mid-August 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning late November 2026 (previously late October) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations with 50 or more Copilot licenses
  • Users assigned the CxO or CxO-delegate role in the Copilot dashboard
  • Organizations using Microsoft Viva Pulse and the Copilot dashboard

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Viva Pulse
  • Copilot dashboard
  • Microsoft Viva Insights

What will happen

  • The feature will be enabled by default for eligible organizations.
  • Survey results appear in your existing Pulse and dashboard surfaces.
  • Authorized users with the CxO or CxO-delegate role can send Viva Pulse surveys to predefined Copilot user cohorts from the Copilot dashboard.
  • Available survey audiences include:
    • All Copilot Licensed Users
    • All Copilot Active Users
  • Survey audiences will be generated using Copilot dashboard data and respect supported dashboard filters.
  • Individual employee identities are not exposed through audience selection.
  • Viva Insights exclusion lists continue to be honored for survey distribution.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to enable this feature.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review who has been assigned the CxO or CxO-delegate role in the Copilot dashboard.
  • Inform change leaders that targeted audience surveys are available.
  • Verify that Viva Insights exclusion lists are current and accurately reflect users who should be excluded from surveys.

Administrators can disable this feature in the Microsoft 365 admin center by navigating to Setup > Microsoft Viva > Feature access management > Viva Pulse and turning off Targeted Audience Surveys.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can disable the feature through Feature access management in Microsoft Viva Pulse.
Does this change affect how users communicate or provide feedback within Microsoft 365?Yes. This feature provides a new method for authorized users to collect employee feedback by sending Viva Pulse surveys to predefined Copilot user audiences from Copilot dashboard.
Does this change process customer or organizational data in a new way?Yes. Survey audiences are generated using Copilot dashboard data and existing audience filters to identify eligible recipients for Viva Pulse surveys.
Can users be assigned access to this feature through role-based permissions?Yes. Only users assigned the CxO or CxO-delegate role in Copilot dashboard can create surveys for the predefined Copilot audiences.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center – Boost contact center efficiency with Real Time Streaming Analytics
item.description:
We are introducing Real-Time Streaming Analytics in the new Contact Center supervisor workspace application, providing supervisors with near real-time visibility into Dynamics 365 Contact Center performance without requiring dashboard refreshes. This feature will be generally available starting Oct 30th with a phased rollout across all regions through November 9, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables supervisors to monitor contact center performance and take action from a single experience. Key capabilities include:
  • Monitor performance in near real-time:Track key metrics such as queue backlog, service level, abandon rate, representative presence, available capacity, and conversations handled over time without refreshing the dashboard.
  • Display live performance on wallboards: View continuously updated metrics in full-screen mode to provide a shared view of contact center performance.
  • Analyze queue and representative performance: Drill down from high-level summaries to queue-level and representative-level views to identify performance changes and potential issues.
  • Take action directly from the dashboard: Adjust representative queues, presence, skills, and capacity profiles within the supervisor experience.
  • Configure performance thresholds: Set thresholds for key metrics and use color-coded indicators to identify At Risk and Critical conditions.
Supervisors and contact center administrators can access the Contact Center Supervisor Workspace through the Supervisor Dashboard URL and connect to their organization to begin monitoring real-time contact center performance.

What do I need to do to prepare?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Boost contact center efficiency with real-time streaming analytics.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Two presenters can share their screens or windows simultaneously in meetings
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Two presenters can share a screen or window at the same time in a Teams meeting. Participants can see both shared content streams simultaneously, making it easier to compare and discuss content from different presenters. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 80239.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This capability will be enabled for all meetings by default, allowing a second presenter to start sharing without requiring the first presenter to stop.

When enabled, participants can see both shared content streams at the same time, creating a more seamless experience for scenarios such as comparing documents, presenting complementary information, or collaborating across multiple sources.

Meeting organizers will also have a meeting option to control whether multiple presenters can share simultaneously in an individual meeting.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Organizations will have tenant-level admin control to determine whether simultaneous sharing is available to their users. Review your organization's sharing policies and inform users and support teams about the new experience.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat
item.description:
[What and why]

We are adding support for external presenters in event group chat, the private chat used by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters for coordination during an event or structured meeting. This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters using event group chat in meetings or events, including external presenters.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Event group chat
  • Meetings and events with the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled

What will happen

  • External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.
  • The meeting or event must have the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled to use event group chat. 
  • External user collaboration must be enabled for external presenters to use this functionality.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change store new customer data?

  • No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

  • Yes. External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat. That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history. The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?

  • Yes. We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters. Both tenants must allow external access.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. External presenters' messages fall under existing federated-chat handling.

  • Affect Connector Analytics

  • Teams Search

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra ID: Reminder to migrate from Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
[What and why]

This is a reminder of the upcoming retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication in Microsoft Entra ID, previously announced in MC1426371 (July 13, 2026) and MC1434201 (GCC, July 20, 2026).

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will retire starting February 1, 2027. Complete your migration before rollout begins to avoid interrupting users' sign-in experience.

SMS and voice are vulnerable to phishing and SIM-swap attacks. Microsoft recommends passkeys for stronger, phishing-resistant protection. You can also migrate to another supported authentication method or retain SMS and voice by configuring a customer-managed telecom provider (CYOT) through the Microsoft Security Store.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Retirement (Worldwide and GCC): Beginning February 1, 2027, and expected to complete in early February 2027.
  • Complete migration or configure CYOT before February 1, 2027, rather than waiting for the rollout to reach your tenant.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations and users that rely on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice authentication
  • Customer-managed telecom providers configured through the Microsoft Security Store are not affected.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID authentication

What will happen

  • Users with another registered sign-in method will use that method. They will not be required to register a passkey to continue signing in.
  • Users whose only registered sign-in method is SMS or voice can use SMS or voice one final time to verify their identity. They must then register a passkey before continuing sign-in.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization uses Microsoft-provided SMS or voice, complete these steps before February 1, 2027:

  • Identify affected users. Review who relies on SMS or voice, especially users with no other registered sign-in method.
  • Complete migration. Help affected users register and start using passkeys or another supported authentication method before rollout begins.
  • Configure CYOT if you need to retain SMS or voice. Configure a customer-managed telecom provider through the Microsoft Security Store before rollout begins.
  • Notify users and your helpdesk. Explain the deadline, required actions, and the passkey-registration requirement for users who only have SMS or voice registered.

If your organization does not use Microsoft-provided SMS or voice, no action is required for this retirement.

Learn more

  • Migration guidance
  • Passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID
  • Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
item.description:
Updated October 27, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early November 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete in late December 2026 (previously mid-December)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

  • Plan a Windows Hello for Business deployment | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Prepare users to provision and use Windows Hello for Business | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) OneDrive for Business: Improved Windows Desktop sync error messages for max path length
item.description:
Updated October 27, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

We are improving the OneDrive sync experience on Windows desktop to provide clearer, more actionable guidance when file and folder paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience will show exactly how many characters a path exceeds the limit and will provide a guided flow to rename or move affected items so they can sync successfully.

This improvement addresses a common OneDrive sync issue by reducing user confusion, minimizing workflow disruption, and helping users resolve errors faster.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557563.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning January 2027 (previously end of October 2026) and expected to complete by end of January 2027 (previously end of November 2026)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All users of the OneDrive sync client on Windows desktop

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business (Windows desktop sync client)

What will happen

Max path errors are one of the most commonly reported issues by OneDrive sync users. Currently, when a file or folder path exceeds the 520-character sync limit, the error message only states how many characters the path exceeds the limit and asks users to shorten it. In addition, File Explorer limitations may prevent users from renaming paths over 260 characters, and the sync client may stop syncing until the issue is resolved.

As part of this improved error experience, when users encounter max path errors, the sync client will continue running and users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience.

With this update:

  • The sync client will continue running when users encounter max path errors
  • Users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience to resolve issues directly

The rename experience will:

  • Show the number of over-limit characters
  • Highlight which items in the path can be renamed
  • Allow renames even when the path exceeds 260 characters

Screenshot - Custom rename dialog

The move experience will:

  • Show over-limit character counts in a guided interface
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit shared items in OneDrive
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit items in shortcuts

Screenshot - Example warning dialog for overlimit items in shortcuts

These enhancements are designed to reduce troubleshooting time and improve the overall sync experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. This update will be automatically available through the OneDrive sync client.

You may want to:

  • Inform your helpdesk and support teams about the improved error messages, as this update should reduce max-path-related support tickets.
  • Update internal documentation for resolving OneDrive sync issues if applicable.

Learn more

  • Fix paths that are too long to sync in OneDrive | Microsoft Support
  • Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. This update does not change how customer data is stored, processed, or accessed.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
(Updated October 16, 2026: Added guidance for managing the Alberta and British Columbia time zone changes in Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia.)

(Updated October 27, 2026: Included reference and link to more guidance published in the Message center post MC1526468.)

[What and why:]

Windows updates are now available to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. On November 1, 2026, clocks in affected regions will not be set back by one hour.

Manitoba will permanently stay on UTC-5, Alberta and affected locations will permanently stay on UTC-6, and most of British Columbia will permanently stay on UTC-7. The new Windows updates add region-specific time zones to support these changes.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • September 22, 2026: The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available in the September 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
  • October 13, 2026: The Manitoba change became available for all supported versions of Windows. The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available for all other supported versions of Windows, including Windows Server. These changes are included in the October 2026 security update.
  • November 1, 2026: The time zone transitions take effect at 2:00 a.m. local time. Clocks in affected areas will not be set back by one hour.

[Impact on your organization:]

Devices in affected regions will display an incorrect local time after the November 1, 2026 transition if the applicable Windows update is not installed or the appropriate time zone is not selected. The updates add the following region-specific time zones:

  • (UTC-05:00) Manitoba
  • (UTC-06:00) Mountain Time (Alberta)
  • (UTC-07:00) Pacific Time (British Columbia)

The Alberta time zone change also applies to Yellowknife and Inuvik in the Northwest Territories and locations in southeastern British Columbia that align with Alberta.

Devices configured to set the time zone automatically will select the appropriate new time zone. On other devices, the new region-specific time zone must be selected manually.

[Action required/recommendations:]

  • Install the applicable Windows update on affected devices before November 1, 2026.
  • Confirm that affected devices use the appropriate region-specific time zone after installing the update.
  • If a device cannot receive the update before November 1, 2026, read and follow the interim guidance for each affected region detailed in the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog and move the device to the appropriate region-specific time zone as soon as possible.

Note: To manage this change in Outlook, please follow the guidance in the article Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia. For guidance on how to manage Outlook and Exchange Online calendar events, Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows, and other potentially impacted Microsoft 365 experiences, see MC1526468.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization and region-specific time zone.

[Additional information:]

  • British Columbia 2026 time zone update available now
  • Manitoba 2026 time zone update available now

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
Updated October 27, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook: Change the organizer of meetings
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing Change organizer for eligible Outlook meetings and recurring meeting series. Users can ask another person in their organization to become the organizer, and the selected person must accept before ownership changes. This supports personal and team productivity by maintaining meeting continuity during role changes, leave, and offboarding.

[Rollout Schedule:]

This phase supports non-online meetings:

  • Worldwide: Early November through early December 2026 
  • GCC: Late November through late December 2026 
  • GCC High: Early December through late December 2026 
  • DoD: Early December through late December 2026 

Phase 2 will add eligible online meetings. For Teams meetings, the transfer will generate a new Teams meeting link owned by the new organizer. Phase 2 will also be rolled out along with phase 1 with the same schedule. 

Phase 3 will add transfer support for eligible Teams meeting artifacts, including chat, meeting options, transcripts, recordings, agenda, notes, and attendance reports. Its timing will be announced separately.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  1. Users who organize eligible meetings or recurring series.
  2. Users selected to become a new organizer.
  3. Delegates with permission to edit meetings on another user's primary calendar.
  4. Help desk teams supporting meeting ownership transitions.

Platforms/Services:

  1. Outlook on the web
  2. New Outlook for Windows
  3. Teams Microsoft 365 Calendar
  4. Exchange Online

Classic Outlook for Windows is not supported.

What will happen:

  1. The current organizer can select one person in the same organization or tenant and send an organizer change request.
  2. The meeting remains with the current organizer until the selected person accepts.
  3. The organizer or an authorized delegate can cancel a pending request.
  4. For recurring series, future instances move to the new organizer's calendar. Earlier instances remain with the previous organizer.
  5. Internal Exchange Online attendees receive a silent update and do not need to respond again. Their Reminder, Category, Show As, and Private settings are preserved.
  6. External and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and a new invitation, which requires a response.
  7. The meeting body, attachments, and sensitivity labels are preserved. The new organizer might require separate access to OneDrive attachments or links.
  8. If the meeting has a Teams meeting, a new Teams meeting link will be generated upon transfer which will be owned by the new organizer.
  9. This feature is enabled by default and requires no tenant configuration. There is no admin setting to control the availability of this feature.

The meeting must be in the future, use a work or school account, and be stored on the organizer's primary calendar. Draft, canceled, encrypted, group calendar, group mailbox, and shared mailbox meetings are not eligible.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No administrative action is required.

  1. Review meeting ownership processes for role changes, leave, and offboarding.
  2. Update internal meeting management and offboarding documentation.
  3. Tell users that the new organizer must accept the request and that the previous organizer is not automatically retained as an attendee.
  4. Advise users that external attendees must respond to a replacement invitation.
  5. Ask users to confirm that the new organizer can access linked OneDrive content.
  6. Review the Microsoft Support article, Change the organizer of a meeting in Outlook.

[Compliance Considerations:]

ConsiderationImpactExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?YesFuture meeting instances move to the new organizer's calendar and can be managed by that organizer. Earlier recurring instances remain with the previous organizer. Meeting content is preserved, but linked OneDrive content might require separate access.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?YesThe feature adds organizer transfer requests within an organization. Internal attendees receive silent updates, while external and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and replacement invitation.

item.title: [planForChange] AI Builder credits retirement: Prepare to use Copilot Credits
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is retiring AI Builder credits and replacing them with Copilot Credits. Organizations using AI Builder must arrange Copilot Credit capacity before their existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire, or sooner if those credits are exhausted, to avoid interruptions.

 AI Builder features are not being retired. They will continue to be supported using Copilot Credits, bringing AI Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio capabilities onto a common credit-based licensing model.

When this will happen:

  • November 1, 2025: Sales of AI Builder capacity add-ons ended for new customers.
  • November 1, 2026: AI Builder capacity add-ons reach end of life. Credits from active add-on contracts remain usable until those contracts expire.
  • November 1, 2026: New or renewed eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses will no longer include seeded AI Builder credits. Seeded credits included with eligible licenses purchased or renewed before this date remain available through the end of the applicable contract term.

November 1, 2026, is not a universal cutoff for existing credits. Your transition deadline depends on when your applicable contracts expire.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This change affects organizations that use AI Builder credits from capacity add-ons or credits included with eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses to run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

  • AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate consume available AI Builder credits first. When those credits are unavailable or exhausted, usage automatically falls back to available Copilot Credits.
  • If neither credit type is available, affected AI Builder runs are blocked, which can interrupt apps, flows, and business processes.
  • AI Builder credits will not automatically convert to Copilot Credits. Consumption rates differ by capability; there is no single conversion ratio.
  • AI Builder features in Copilot Studio already consume Copilot Credits.
  • This change affects licensing, not feature availability. Administrators must ensure sufficient capacity to continue running AI Builder features.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Admin action is required before November 1, 2026, for organizations with AI Builder capacity add-ons, and before existing credit entitlements expire to prevent disruption.

  1. Review your contracts. Identify when your AI Builder capacity add-ons and licenses providing seeded credits expire. For AI Builder capacity add-ons, turn off automatic renewal in the Microsoft 365 admin center or work with your partner to do so in Partner Center.
  2. Review credit consumption across environments. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Download reports > + New > AI Builder. Generate and download the report to review credits consumed by date, user, and environment during the 30 days preceding the selected target date.
  3.  3.** Identify affected workloads.** In the Power Automate portal, select the environment, then go to Automation Center > Monitor > AI Builder activity. Makers can review their own activity for models they can access; users with the System Administrator or System Customizer role can review all activity in the environment. Activity data is also available in the AI Event table in Dataverse.
  4. Plan replacement capacity. Use the AI Builder capability rate table to estimate Copilot Credit requirements. Purchase and make sufficient Copilot Credits available to affected environments before existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire. Do not assume that the same number of Copilot Credits will cover your current AI Builder credit usage.
  5. Notify makers and support teams. Update internal licensing guidance and identify business-critical apps and flows that could be interrupted by insufficient capacity.

  • AI Builder consumption report
  • Monitor AI Builder activity

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages

Platforms and services

  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Users will soon be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor authentication method. Previously, people had to set up an alternate MFA method like SMS or Voice before they could add a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO. That extra step pushed users toward weaker methods and slowed the move to phishing-resistant sign-in. Now password-only users can go straight to a passkey, making it easier to adopt strong authentication from day one. As part of this work, we will also be enabling Authenticator App passwordless sign-in to be a user's first registered MFA method. 

[Rollout schedule]

This feature will roll out in phases: 

Phase 1: Support for synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows, and FIDO2 security keys.  

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by early January 2027 (previously late November 2026). 

Phase 2: Support for Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator App passkey, and Authenticator App passwordless sign-in. 

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early January 2026 and expect to complete by late February 2027. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have not yet registered a multifactor authentication method
  • Identity and security administrators responsible for authentication onboarding and registration policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Passkeys (FIDO2)
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Microsoft Authenticator passwordless sign-in

What will happen

  • Password-only users will be able to register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first MFA method.
  • Users will no longer need to register a method such as SMS or voice before registering a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, or Authenticator passwordless sign-in.
  • Organizations may see reduced registration friction and increased adoption of phishing-resistant authentication methods.
  • Users who are enabled for passkeys will be prompted to register a passkey by default when completing applicable registration experiences, including those triggered by multifactor authentication (MFA) enforcement and Conditional Access authentication strengths. Security Defaults MFA registration prompts will adopt this experience in January–February 2027.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required for this change.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review Conditional Access policies related to security information registration.
  • Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.
  • Review your user onboarding and registration guidance and update it as needed to reflect that eligible users may be prompted to register a passkey by default.

Learn more 

  • (To be updated closer to rollout) Register a synced passkey (FIDO2) | Authentication | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can control which authentication methods users are allowed to register through existing Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access policies.
Does the change affect access or authentication controls?Yes. The update changes how users register multifactor authentication methods by allowing eligible users to register supported passkeys or passwordless authentication methods as their first MFA method.
Can administrators govern the feature through existing Microsoft Entra controls?Yes. Administrators retain control over the feature through Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access configurations.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Update to MC1510951: Canada 2026 time zone changes — Microsoft 365 impact and required admin actions
item.description:
This post updates MC1510951 ((Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada, posted October 16, 2026).

On November 1, 2026, affected locations in British Columbia, Alberta, and Manitoba will not move clocks back and will remain on UTC-07:00, UTC-06:00, and UTC-05:00 respectively. Affected locations in the Northwest Territories (including Yellowknife and Inuvik) align with the Alberta change, and Northwestern Ontario aligns with the Manitoba change.

Windows and Microsoft 365 services depend on updated time zone definitions for correct scheduling and display behavior.

How this affects your organization

Confirmed impact

  1. Outlook and Exchange Online (calendar): Users must move to the new time zone. Existing events do not migrate automatically. Recurring meetings require additional review.
  2. Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: Some devices may display time one hour behind Windows until Edge/WebView2 is updated.

Potential impact (under validation)

  1. Microsoft Teams (desktop, web, mobile) and other Teams devices
  2. Outlook for iOS, Android, and Mac
  3. Microsoft Bookings
  4. Shifts
  5. SharePoint Online
  6. OneDrive

What you need to do

  1. Ensure Windows devices in affected regions have the latest Windows updates (including October 2026 updates).
  2. Ask users in affected regions to select the new time zone in Outlook and review meetings scheduled after November 1, especially recurring series.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot for Teams: Bilingual consecutive interpretation mode with Interpreter agent

[Introduction]

Consecutive Interpretation is a new interpretation mode available as an add‑on to the existing Interpreter agent in Microsoft Teams. It enables structured multilingual conversations in meetings by providing shared, meeting‑level interpretation when enabled by a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user.

This mode uses consecutive (turn‑by‑turn) interpretation, meaning participants speak one at a time and each speaker's words are interpreted before the next speaker begins. This structured flow reduces overlap, improves interpretation accuracy, and helps everyone stay aligned in real time.

Consecutive Interpretation is ideal for back‑and‑forth, interactive discussions where participants need to respond, clarify, and build on each other’s input across languages, such as working sessions, negotiations, and cross‑functional collaboration.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

If no corrective action is initiated after repeated notifications, when a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 90 days from the date the tenant exceeds capacity, affected sandbox environments will be disabled and will no longer be accessible to users. During this phase customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed.

Production environments are not subject to administration mode and disabled stage restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox or production type environments will remain blocked while the tenant is over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 14, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The following products are included in the storage validation rollout:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox and production type environments are blocked immediately when the tenant exceeds its entitled capacity.
2. Administration mode After 30 unresolved days from T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 90 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from accessing *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation. During this phase, customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed. All other mechanisms designed to resolve overage are also available to customers at this phase.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant’s current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, future restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Admins can exit Administration Mode at any time; however, the overage lifecycle continues as long as the tenant remains over its entitled storage capacity. Once the tenant returns below 100%, no further restrictions are applied. Environments do not automatically return to their previous state; admins must manually exit Administration Mode or re-enable them, as applicable. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing are excluded from the overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Invite makers and users to become aware of these potential restrictions and to notify administrators about possible areas of adjustment.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:
  • What happens when my organization exceeds storage capacity?
  • Dataverse capacity-based storage details
  • Manage data with Dataverse governance policies
  • Free up storage space
  • Add more Dataverse capacity
  • Configure pay-as-you-go in your environment
  • What environments consume tenant capacity
  • Power Platform licensing guidance
*Affected environments: Sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go enabled. Any references to affected environments in this message apply exclusively to those sandbox environments

item.title: [stayInformed] Teams admin center - Intelligent insights for meeting quality
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Gain proactive visibility into meeting quality across your organization with AI-powered insights in Teams admin center that identify emerging patterns, highlight impacted users and locations, and surface likely causes with recommended actions. This helps IT administrators detect and address issues earlier, improve meeting quality, and stay ahead of potential disruptions.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Administrators will find new enhancements to the meeting and call troubleshooting flow in Teams admin center. Administrators can find these insights in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meetings. The experience evaluates historical meeting-quality data across the organization and highlights locations or public IPs where meeting quality is behaving unusually.

When an anomaly is detected, administrators will be able to:

  • Identify meeting-quality hotspots across locations and public IPs and see how many users are affected.
  • Review quality trends to understand how meeting quality has changed over time.
  • Understand likely root causes across network factors such as bandwidth, Wi-Fi, VPN and proxy; compute factors such as CPU, memory and client; and devices such as microphones, cameras and speakers.
  • Take recommended actions based on the likely cause and severity of the issue.
  • Review affected users and supporting evidence to better understand the scope and impact of the anomaly.

Insights are refreshed daily and use machine learning to dynamically evaluate what constitutes anomalous behavior, so administrators don’t need to configure thresholds.

The insights use meeting data across the tenant and supported clients and platforms. They do not include meeting telemetry from SIP phones or telemetry from PSTN and peer-to-peer calls.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No configuration is required. Once available in your tenant, navigate to Teams admin center > Meetings > Meetings to start reviewing insights. The experience is available to Global Administrators, Teams Administrators, Teams Communications Administrators, Teams Communications Support Engineers, and Teams Communications Support Specialists.

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature uses AI/machine learning to analyze historical meeting-quality data and surface insights to admins; it does not alter how customer data is stored or processed. Review your organization’s data and AI governance policies as appropriate.
